title: Compound Words
keyIdea: A compound word is two whole words joined to make one new word: sun + shine = sunshine. Each part keeps all its letters, so ear + ring = earring, with two r's. To read or spell a compound, find the two words inside it. The meanings of the two words help with the new meaning, and the last word usually says what the thing is: a goldfish is a fish. A word that only hides little words, like carpet, is not a compound.
familyTip: Go on a compound word hunt at home: toothbrush, bedroom, cupboard, doorbell, teapot. For each one, say the two words inside it and what they tell you. Then make up silly ones together, like a spoonbath or a sockhat, and ask whether they are real words or made-up ones.

visual.caption: Is it a compound word? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: glue two words into one, cut compounds at the join, order the parts, sort real compounds from tricks, find real rain words.

kid: Some words are made of two words stuck together. Sun and shine make sunshine. Foot and ball make football. We call them compound words.
When you join the two words, keep every letter. Ear ends with r and ring starts with r. So earring has two r's. Write the first word, then the second word, with no gap.
To read a long word, look for the two words inside it. Toothbrush is tooth and brush. Cut it where both parts are real words. Too and thbrush does not work.

The two words help you know what the new word means. The last word tells you what the thing is. A houseboat is a boat you live in. A boathouse is a house for boats. Carpet has car and pet in it, but it is not a car or a pet, so it is not a compound.
adult: Ages 5 to 8. This matches the National Curriculum in England, English Appendix 1, Year 1 spelling: compound words are two words joined together, and each part of the longer word is spelt as it would be on its own (football, playground, farmyard, bedroom, blackberry). It also matches CCSS L.2.4d: use the meaning of each word to predict the meaning of a compound (birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly). Key words: compound word, root word, morpheme, closed compound, head word, syllable.

Most compounds children meet early are closed compounds, written as one word. In English the second part is usually the head: it names the kind of thing, and the first part narrows it down. So a goldfish is a fish and a houseboat is a boat, and swapping the parts changes the meaning. Some compounds are written with a space (ice cream) or a hyphen, and a few do not name their last part (a pickpocket is a person), but the joined, head-final kind is the one to teach first.

Common mistakes: dropping a letter where the words meet (earing for earring); splitting a compound in the wrong place when reading (too-thbrush); calling any long word with a little word inside a compound (carpet, button, season, target); writing the parts in the wrong order or with a gap; and making up a compound that is not a real word (rainsit). The lab, the practice and the challenge target each of these.

In the lab your child glues sun, foot and ear onto shine, ball and ring, and sees that earring keeps both r's. They cut cupcake, snowman, toothbrush and bedroom at the join, put house and boat in order for two different clues, sort playground, farmyard and blackberry from carpet, button and season, and find which endings make real words with rain. Words are said aloud when tapped, if the device can speak.

practice.hint: Find a whole word at the start, then a whole word at the end.
practice.explain: Sunshine is sun + shine. Both parts are real words, and the sun is what shines.

practice.prompt: You write {n} compound words. Each one is made of 2 words. How many small words did you join?
practice.hint: Each compound word has 2 small words in it. Count 2 for every compound.
practice.explain: {n} compound words with 2 small words in each is {=2*n} small words.

practice.prompt: Ear + ring. Which spelling is right?
practice.hint: Keep every letter of ear and every letter of ring, with no gap.
practice.explain: Earring keeps the r at the end of ear and the r at the start of ring, so it has two r's.

practice.prompt: Sam sees {n} snowmen in the park. Where do you cut the word snowman?
practice.hint: Cut where both parts are whole words you know.
practice.explain: Snow and man are both real words, and a snowman is a man made of snow.

choices: No, a carpet is not a car or a pet
Yes, it has car and pet in it
Yes, because it is a long word
practice.hint: Do the two little words help you know what a carpet is?
practice.explain: Car and pet hide in carpet, but they do not tell you what a carpet is. So carpet is not a compound.

pool.prompt: Which word is a compound word?
pool.hint: Look for two whole words that help the meaning.
pool.explain: A playground is ground where you play: play + ground. Button and season only hide little words.

choices: Gold that looks like a fish
pool.hint: The last word tells you what the thing is.
pool.explain: Fish is the last word, so a goldfish is a kind of fish. Gold tells you what colour it is.

pool.prompt: Foot + ball. How do you write the new word?
pool.hint: Keep every letter and leave no gap.
pool.explain: Football is foot and ball joined with no gap, and every letter stays.

pool.prompt: Rain can start {n} compound words, like raincoat. You find 1 more. How many rain words do you know now?
pool.hint: Count on 1 from the words you already know.
pool.explain: {n} and 1 more is {=n+1} compound words that start with rain.

pool.prompt: Which ending makes a real compound word with rain?
pool.hint: Say each one: rain + drop, rain + sit, rain + pen. Which is a real word?
pool.explain: A raindrop is a drop of rain. Rainsit and rainpen are not real words.

pool.prompt: A birdhouse is a house for a bird. What is a houseboat?
choices: A boat you can live in
A house next to a boat
pool.hint: The last word says what the thing is.
pool.explain: Boat is the last word, so a houseboat is a boat, one that people live in like a house.

pool.prompt: There are {n} cupcakes on a plate. Which two words make cupcake?
pool.hint: Find the two words you know inside it.
pool.explain: Cupcake is cup + cake: a little cake, often baked in a paper cup.

choices: Two whole words joined into one
pool.hint: Think of sunshine. What is it made of?
pool.explain: A compound word is two whole words joined into one new word, like sun + shine.

pool.prompt: Which word has little words hiding in it but is NOT a compound?
pool.hint: Do the little words help you know what it means?
pool.explain: Tar and get hide in target, but a target is not tar or get. Bedroom and farmyard are real compounds.
